## Appearance

Wilfred Mott is noted for having hands that feel perpetually cold and fish-like.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Farewell P23](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0023)_

## Personality

Wilfred Mott is a character driven by a strong ambition to enter politics and serve as a member of Parliament. By his sophomore year, he displays an increasingly pompous demeanor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Regent’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v3 ch.Relationships P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)_

## History

Wilfred Mott previously penned pieces for the local newspaper. In his youth, he once declared to his mother that [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) was the cleverest female student in school, and he defeated [Elias Purdy MacKinnon](../character/elias-purdy-mackinnon.md) in a fight after Elias made a remark about her. He also challenged Arty Pettigrew to leap across a well during a Mayflower picking trip, and he shared a family memory that his grandmother saw his deceased grandfather herding cows a year after his burial. Wilfred later traveled by train and ferry alongside [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) as they departed for [Portmaris](../codex/places.md#portmaris). While attending college, he joined [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), [Honora Hollis](../character/honora-hollis.md), Hugh, and [Cressida Lindsay](../character/cressy-lindsay.md) on a walk along [Linden Avenue](../codex/places.md#linden-avenue). During Nell's term at [Wexcombe](../codex/places.md#wexcombe-college), Wilfred proposed to her, but his proposal was met with displeasure and rejected.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong P29](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0029), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v2 XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country P0](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0000), [v3 ch.Farewell P0](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0000), +11 more_
